Bob Odenkirk has never won an Emmy for playing Jimmy McGill and Saul Goodman in Better Call Saul, despite receiving six nominations for Outstanding Lead Actor in a Drama Series.

Vince Gilligan's creative run has produced some of the most celebrated television in modern history, but the Emmy awards tell a surprisingly bittersweet story. While Breaking Bad cemented its legacy with 16 wins out of 58 nominations, his newest venture Pluribus is already off to a dominant start, taking home 6 Emmys from 18 nominations at the 2026 ceremony.

Yet, the tragedy of Better Call Saul remains one of the Television Academy's biggest modern snubs. Despite earning 53 nominations over its six-season run, with Bob Odenkirk never won an Emmy for playing Jimmy McGill, despite receiving six nominations for Outstanding Lead Actor in a Drama Series. The prequel series ended without a single victory. Does an Emmy count actually define a masterclass series, or did Better Call Saul deserve way better? Let us know in the comments!
